findings.title: Reschedules still bypass the deferred cancellation mechanism
findings.body: handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true for every reschedule, so this branch immediately cancels the SendGrid batch rather than recording it for cron. SendGrid retains these cancellations until the original send dates, so 100 future reschedule cancellations still exhaust the limit that caused this bug. Subsequent POST failures are only logged, and cancelled=true is never persisted for cron to retry. Old reminders can therefore still be delivered after rescheduling.

findings.title: Cancel imminent reminders before waiting for cron
findings.body: Scheduled-email cancellations now only set cancelled=true, even when the send time is close. With the 15-minute cron interval, a reminder due at 12:24 and cancelled at 12:01 after the 12:00 run is not processed until 12:15. It is then inside SendGrid's ten-minute no-cancellation window, although an immediate cancellation would have succeeded. These reminders will still be sent; near-term batches need immediate cancellation rather than unconditional deferral.

findings.title: Isolate failures and commit each successful cancellation
findings.body: The entire cancellation loop shares one try/catch, and database deletes are deferred until every SendGrid POST succeeds. Prisma queries are lazy, so if any POST rejects, none of the queued deletes execute and every remaining reminder is skipped. A repeatedly failing batch can keep aborting subsequent runs, while successfully cancelled batches are unnecessarily submitted again. Valid reminders can miss their cancellation windows and be delivered. Handle errors per reminder and execute each successful reminder's delete before moving on.

findings.title: Await the reminder cancellation writes before returning
findings.body: The promises returned by both cancellation helpers are discarded, while the previously awaited reminder database deletions have been removed. These helpers now perform the only write that marks a scheduled email cancelled or removes an unscheduled reminder. The handler can therefore return success before those writes commit; a serverless invocation can finish with cancellation work still pending, leaving reminders active. Collect and await the helper promises, including the equivalent changed call sites.
